title: All Nodes Distance K in Binary Tree
description:
Given the `root` of a binary tree, a `target` node in the tree, and an integer `k`, return a list of the values of all nodes that have a distance `k` from the `target` node.

Distance between two nodes is defined as the number of edges on the unique path connecting them. You may return the answer in **any order**.

All node values in the tree are unique, and `target` is guaranteed to be a node in the tree.
constraints: The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [1, 500].
All the values Node.val are unique.
target is the value of one of the nodes in the tree.
hints: A tree becomes an undirected graph as soon as each node also knows its parent.
Run a DFS or BFS from `root` to record a `parent` map from each node to its parent.
Then perform a level-order BFS starting from `target` (tracking visited nodes), expanding to `left`, `right`, and `parent`. After `k` levels, the nodes remaining in the queue are exactly the answer.

examples.explanation: The nodes at distance 2 from target node 5 are 7, 4 (descendants) and 1 (via parent 3).
The tree only has node 1, so no nodes are at distance 3 from it.
At distance 0 from node 1, the only node is node 1 itself.

inputs.name: root
inputs.description: Level-order array representation of the binary tree
